# Where Novis deliberately differs from PHP

Every rule carrying a `divergesFromPhp` note, with the rule that owns it. Generated from `docs/rules/` by `python tools/rules.py --render`.

| Topic | Divergence | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Errors | an exception is a status value checked after every call, not a stack unwind | [`errors/propagation`](rules/errors.md#errors-propagation) |
| Errors | throwing is not a performance cliff, so exceptions may be used on ordinary control-flow paths | [`errors/throw-is-not-slower`](rules/errors.md#errors-throw-is-not-slower) |
| Errors | `catch (Throwable)` provably cannot see a resource-limit fatal; `Exception` and `Error` are not class names | [`errors/throwable-hierarchy`](rules/errors.md#errors-throwable-hierarchy) |
| Errors | every failure category ends in a log line, and no handler is ever given a second attempt at the same failure | [`errors/escalation-ladder`](rules/errors.md#errors-escalation-ladder) |
| Errors | the handler is request-local rather than global, and runs on a reserve carved out before execution started | [`errors/on-limit`](rules/errors.md#errors-on-limit) |
| Errors | recursion is bounded by an 8 MB native stack rather than by `memory_limit`, so deep PHP recursion needs a rewrite | [`errors/stack-depth`](rules/errors.md#errors-stack-depth) |
| Errors | the handler is request-local and fires exactly once; there is no global `set_exception_handler` | [`errors/on-uncaught-throw`](rules/errors.md#errors-on-uncaught-throw) |
| Errors | there is one model behind every diagnostic, so a value's type is never lost the way `print_r` loses it | [`errors/diagnostic-record`](rules/errors.md#errors-diagnostic-record) |
| Errors | five levels rather than PSR-3's eight, because nobody has a rule for choosing `notice` over `info` | [`errors/log-level`](rules/errors.md#errors-log-level) |
| Errors | one member replaces `var_dump`, `print_r`, `var_export` and `json_encode`, and reads correctly in every medium | [`errors/renderings`](rules/errors.md#errors-renderings) |
| Errors | a cut, a cycle and a redaction are nodes in the record, so every rendering agrees on them instead of truncating per formatter | [`errors/record-transformations`](rules/errors.md#errors-record-transformations) |
| Errors | a forgotten dump writes a log line; the spelling that puts it in a production response does not exist | [`errors/debug-dump`](rules/errors.md#errors-debug-dump) |
| Errors | no `__debugInfo` and no `__toString` in a dump — a dump shows declared state and never a prettier view of it | [`errors/no-render-hook`](rules/errors.md#errors-no-render-hook) |
| Errors | nothing is normalised, unfolded, mangled or truncated into an interpretation | [`errors/ambiguous-input-refused`](rules/errors.md#errors-ambiguous-input-refused) |
| Errors | the outbound half is held to the same list, with no per-call opt-out | [`errors/http-message-defects`](rules/errors.md#errors-http-message-defects) |
| Errors | no `.`-and-space mangling of cookie names, and `__Host-`/`__Secure-` are enforced by the runtime rather than by every read site | [`errors/cookie-name-bytes`](rules/errors.md#errors-cookie-name-bytes) |
| Errors | Windows device names, trailing dots and 8.3 short names are refused on Linux and macOS too | [`errors/path-component-refusals`](rules/errors.md#errors-path-component-refusals) |
| Enums | an enum is not a class in disguise — a case is a compile-time constant, with no singleton, no allocation and no identity | [`enums/closed-integer-type`](rules/enums.md#enums-closed-integer-type) |
| Enums | every case has an integer value even where none is written, so PHP's valueless pure case does not exist | [`enums/declaration`](rules/enums.md#enums-declaration) |
| Enums | `case Hearts = 1;` is not a spelling this language has — an enum body is a comma list | [`enums/no-case-keyword`](rules/enums.md#enums-no-case-keyword) |
| Enums | there is no pure enum and no `string`-backed enum, and `BackedEnum` and `UnitEnum` do not exist | [`enums/one-backing-type`](rules/enums.md#enums-one-backing-type) |
| Enums | no methods, no interfaces, no enum constants, and no `::cases()`, `::from()`, `::tryFrom()`, `->value` or `->name` | [`enums/no-class-machinery`](rules/enums.md#enums-no-class-machinery) |
| Enums | a case is a scalar, so it copies across an isolate boundary like an `int` and has no identity to preserve | [`enums/representation`](rules/enums.md#enums-representation) |
| Enums | there are no case instances for a description to hand back — it carries the type's name and its case list, and nothing that acts | [`enums/reflection`](rules/enums.md#enums-reflection) |
| Iteration | no `rewind()`, `key()`, `valid()` or `IteratorAggregate`, and none of the ~20 SPL iterator classes; a cursor has two members and no key half | [`iteration/two-interfaces`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-two-interfaces) |
| Iteration | reading a cursor before it has advanced, or after it is drained, is an error rather than a `null` or a stale element | [`iteration/cursor-out-of-range`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-cursor-out-of-range) |
| Iteration | an object is iterable only by declaring `Iterable<T>` or `Iterator<T>`; walking an ordinary object's public properties does not compile | [`iteration/foreach-subjects`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-foreach-subjects) |
| Iteration | `ArrayAccess` and `Countable` do not exist; a collection exposes `->get($k)`, `->set($k, $v)` and `->count()` instead | [`iteration/no-magic-collection-interfaces`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-no-magic-collection-interfaces) |
| Iteration | a generator is a compiled state machine rather than a suspended stack, so it costs one small object and behaves the same on every compile target | [`iteration/generators`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-generators) |
| Iteration | a helper called from a generator cannot yield into it; delegation is written as a `foreach` that re-yields | [`iteration/yield-lexical-confinement`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-yield-lexical-confinement) |
| Iteration | no `yield from`, no `send()`, no `throw()` into a generator, no keyed `yield`, and no generator return value to retrieve | [`iteration/one-way-only`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-one-way-only) |
| Programs | existing PHP packages, frameworks and code do not run, and no document may imply otherwise | [`programs/no-compatibility-promise`](rules/programs.md#programs-no-compatibility-promise) |
| Programs | there is no `spl_autoload_register`, no `__autoload` and no `new $name` — a name held in a string can never reach a file | [`programs/no-runtime-autoload`](rules/programs.md#programs-no-runtime-autoload) |
| Programs | the map is a declaration in source rather than a registered loader or a `psr-4` manifest, and it travels with the code instead of with the deployment | [`programs/autoload`](rules/programs.md#programs-autoload) |
| Programs | PSR-4 imposes this by convention; here it is a diagnostic | [`programs/one-declaration-per-autoloaded-file`](rules/programs.md#programs-one-declaration-per-autoloaded-file) |
| Programs | `require` does not inherit the filesystem's case behaviour, so a path that resolves on Windows or macOS resolves on Linux or fails on all three | [`programs/path-case`](rules/programs.md#programs-path-case) |
| Programs | a plugin roster is a compile-time array literal, not a `foreach` over `new $className` | [`programs/implementing`](rules/programs.md#programs-implementing) |
| Programs | the ORM, the service container, the facade, the route cache and the autoload dump have no equivalent, and each is absent by construction rather than by omission | [`programs/framework-refusals`](rules/programs.md#programs-framework-refusals) |
| Statements | `static int $calls = 0;` inside a function and `global $x;` are both parse-time refusals, each naming a class static, a constant or a parameter as the replacement | [`statements/no-function-static-and-no-global`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-function-static-and-no-global) |
| Statements | there is no global constant and no superglobal, so nothing holds state without a declaration a reader can find | [`statements/storage-that-outlives-a-call`](rules/statements.md#statements-storage-that-outlives-a-call) |
| Statements | a closure that never names `$this` is unbound, and `bindTo()`/`bind()` on it return an equivalent closure rather than rebinding anything | [`statements/a-closure-binds-this-only-where-it-uses-it`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-closure-binds-this-only-where-it-uses-it) |
| Statements | `$_SERVER`, `$_GET`, `$_POST`, `$_COOKIE`, `$_FILES`, `$_SESSION`, `$_ENV`, `$argv` and `$argc` do not exist as variables at all | [`statements/no-host-populated-variables`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-host-populated-variables) |
| Statements | neither gets a `Core` class, so `extract($_GET)`-shaped code has no straight-line conversion | [`statements/globals-and-request-are-dropped-outright`](rules/statements.md#statements-globals-and-request-are-dropped-outright) |
| Statements | `use Foo\Bar as Baz;` is a diagnostic, and no function anywhere registers a second name for a class | [`statements/nothing-gets-a-second-name`](rules/statements.md#statements-nothing-gets-a-second-name) |
| Statements | a relative qualified name (`Models\User` inside `namespace App;`) names nothing, and a namespace-prefix import reaches nothing under it | [`statements/a-qualified-name-is-absolute`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-qualified-name-is-absolute) |
| Statements | there is no fallback to the root namespace, so a namespaced file that catches writes `use Throwable;` | [`statements/no-fallback-to-the-root-namespace`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-fallback-to-the-root-namespace) |
| Statements | `\App\Models\User`, `use \App\Models\User;` and `namespace \App;` are each refused rather than accepted and ignored | [`statements/a-leading-separator-does-not-parse`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-leading-separator-does-not-parse) |
| Statements | `include`, `include_once` and `require_once` are parse-time refusals — there is no warn-and-continue and no repeat guard | [`statements/require-is-the-only-inclusion-construct`](rules/statements.md#statements-require-is-the-only-inclusion-construct) |
| Statements | an included file cannot see the includer's locals, and the includer cannot see its own | [`statements/a-required-file-shares-declarations-not-locals`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-required-file-shares-declarations-not-locals) |
| Statements | `die` and `die('bye')` do not compile; `exit` is the exact replacement | [`statements/exit-is-the-only-termination-keyword`](rules/statements.md#statements-exit-is-the-only-termination-keyword) |
| Statements | a file opening with `<?php` reports a diagnostic, though the code after the tag still parses | [`statements/nvs-is-the-only-open-tag`](rules/statements.md#statements-nvs-is-the-only-open-tag) |
| Statements | `&$x` is not a by-reference marker; the word is `inout` and it goes before the type | [`statements/inout-is-the-by-reference-spelling`](rules/statements.md#statements-inout-is-the-by-reference-spelling) |
| Statements | PHP removed call-time by-reference in 5.4 and left the caller no marker at all; here the marker is mandatory in both directions | [`statements/inout-is-written-at-the-call`](rules/statements.md#statements-inout-is-written-at-the-call) |
| Statements | `&` keeps only bitwise AND, logical AND and the intersection type; every by-reference spelling of it is a diagnostic | [`statements/ampersand-is-not-a-by-reference-marker`](rules/statements.md#statements-ampersand-is-not-a-by-reference-marker) |
| Attributes | an attribute is never an object — PHP builds a real one the first time `ReflectionAttribute::newInstance()` is called, and needs a declared `#[Attribute]` class for every attribute kind | [`attributes/inert-metadata`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-inert-metadata) |
| Attributes | a named attribute resolves to a `type` alias rather than to a class, so there is no per-attribute-kind declaration and no second namespace of attribute names | [`attributes/attach-sites-and-forms`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-attach-sites-and-forms) |
| Attributes | PHP admits any expression as an attribute argument, `new` included, so building one has an execution order and side effects | [`attributes/payload-is-a-compile-time-constant`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-payload-is-a-compile-time-constant) |
| Attributes | repeatability is the default and needs no `Attribute::IS_REPEATABLE` marker | [`attributes/repeatable`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-repeatable) |
| Attributes | there is no `ReflectionAttribute` and no lookup by attribute class name; two unrelated libraries can ask for the same shape without agreeing on a name | [`attributes/structural-retrieval`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-structural-retrieval) |
| Attributes | "which one did I get?" for a repeated attribute is a diagnostic at the call site rather than a question a test run answers, and no reflection table reaches the compiled unit | [`attributes/retrieval-folds-while-checking`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-retrieval-folds-while-checking) |
| Attributes | `Foo::BAR < X > ($y)` reads as a call carrying a type argument where PHP reads two comparisons | [`attributes/call-site-type-argument`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-call-site-type-argument) |
| Attributes | an annotation that disagrees with the handler is a compile error rather than a documentation bug nobody notices | [`attributes/api-adds-and-cannot-contradict`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-api-adds-and-cannot-contradict) |
| Attributes | no PHP framework can refuse to build a route whose author wrote no access decision | [`attributes/access-is-a-required-sibling`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-access-is-a-required-sibling) |
| Testing | there is no test framework to install, no naming convention and no base class; a malformed test is a compile error rather than a case that silently never runs | [`testing/test-attribute`](rules/testing.md#testing-test-attribute) |
| Testing | total isolation is the default rather than a per-case escape hatch; a static one test wrote is never visible to the next | [`testing/isolate-per-test`](rules/testing.md#testing-isolate-per-test) |
| Testing | test code is absent from a built artifact by construction, rather than excluded by whatever the deployment happened to copy | [`testing/tests-never-reach-a-build`](rules/testing.md#testing-tests-never-reach-a-build) |
| Testing | the argument order is `(actual, expected)`, the reverse of PHPUnit's, and comparing an `int` against a `string` does not compile | [`testing/assertions-are-typed`](rules/testing.md#testing-assertions-are-typed) |
| Testing | a `catch (Throwable)` around a failing assertion cannot turn a red test green; the runner reads its own ledger rather than the exception state | [`testing/failure-ledger`](rules/testing.md#testing-failure-ledger) |
| Testing | there is no `setUp`, `setUpBeforeClass` or `tearDownAfterClass`; the constructor is the only one, and every property is assigned before any test body runs | [`testing/constructor-is-setup`](rules/testing.md#testing-constructor-is-setup) |
| Testing | shared setup is resolved by declared type while compiling, so an unsatisfiable parameter is a diagnostic rather than a null at run time | [`testing/fixtures`](rules/testing.md#testing-fixtures) |
| Testing | a data provider is a checked attribute payload rather than an `array<array<mixed>>` a method returns, so a row that does not fit the signature is refused where it is written | [`testing/data-rows`](rules/testing.md#testing-data-rows) |
| Testing | no class is generated and no source is evaluated; a double is a value the checker compares against the interface, and a loose or nice double is not expressible | [`testing/doubles`](rules/testing.md#testing-doubles) |
| Testing | there is no `expects()`; the method being asserted on is a compile-checked reference, so renaming it breaks the test rather than leaving it passing | [`testing/interaction-after-the-fact`](rules/testing.md#testing-interaction-after-the-fact) |
| Testing | time and randomness are controlled by a declaration on the test rather than by a clock parameter threaded through every time-aware class | [`testing/determinism-declared-on-the-test`](rules/testing.md#testing-determinism-declared-on-the-test) |
| Testing | an HTTP test needs no socket, no port and no web server; the real route table and the real middleware chain answer it in microseconds | [`testing/in-process-request`](rules/testing.md#testing-in-process-request) |
| Testing | there is no reflection to reach a private member with, so white-box testing is bought by co-location and by nothing else | [`testing/private-in-the-same-file`](rules/testing.md#testing-private-in-the-same-file) |
| Testing | a test with no assertion is a failure rather than a risky-marked pass, and a case that only passed on a retry never counts as green | [`testing/runner-is-strict`](rules/testing.md#testing-runner-is-strict) |
| Testing | there is no instrumented build and no extension to load; the probes are compiled into every unit and a bit is flipped on a request already in flight | [`testing/debug-probes`](rules/testing.md#testing-debug-probes) |
| Expressions | the implicit conversion to `bool` is confined to six positions, where PHP applies it wherever a `bool` is wanted | [`expressions/truthy-positions`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-truthy-positions) |
| Expressions | `bytes` has no PHP neighbour and takes emptiness alone, so a one-octet `"0"` buffer is truthy where the string `"0"` is falsy | [`expressions/truthy-table`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-truthy-table) |
| Expressions | the low-precedence keyword connectives are gone entirely, and `xor` has no operator replacement at all | [`expressions/no-keyword-logical-operators`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-no-keyword-logical-operators) |
| Expressions | one of PHP's two destructuring spellings is refused, so `list($a, $b) = $pair;` is a diagnostic naming the bracket form | [`expressions/bracket-destructuring`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-bracket-destructuring) |
| Expressions | a malformed pattern, URI, duration or format string is a compile error at the offset inside the literal, rather than a throw on the first request that reaches the call | [`expressions/intrinsic-literals`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-intrinsic-literals) |
| Expressions | a failed conversion is a `null` the caller tests, where `(int)$x` — which does not parse at all — answered `0` and said nothing | [`expressions/nullable-conversion`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-nullable-conversion) |
| Expressions | there is no operator downcast: `$s as ?Core\Uri` is a compile error rather than a cast, and text reaches a class only through that class's own reader | [`expressions/nullable-conversion-availability`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-nullable-conversion-availability) |
| Expressions | no validator sits next to a parser the way `filter_var` sits next to `parse_url`; `tryParse` is `parse` with the throw caught, so the two can never read one string differently | [`expressions/try-parse`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-try-parse) |
| Expressions | there is no loose-versus-strict pair to pick between — one operator, which never converts either operand | [`expressions/one-equality-operator`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-one-equality-operator) |
| Expressions | `"1" == 1` neither answers `true` nor `false`; it does not compile, and the diagnostic names the conversion the author meant | [`expressions/disjoint-comparison-refused`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-disjoint-comparison-refused) |
| Expressions | each row where PHP's two operators disagreed takes `===`'s answer — two strings compare as text and never as numbers, and an array compares in key order | [`expressions/equality-semantics`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-equality-semantics) |
| Expressions | PHP's `==` walked properties; here there is no property walk, no `__equals`, no `equals()` protocol and no `Equatable` interface | [`expressions/object-identity-equality`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-object-identity-equality) |
| Expressions | a cross-type pairing is `false` rather than PHP's converting comparison, and it is the one place a comparison answers instead of refusing to compile | [`expressions/mixed-equality`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-mixed-equality) |
| Expressions | `switch` no longer compares loosely while `match` compares identically — there is one comparison, and both use it | [`expressions/switch-match-equality`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-switch-match-equality) |
| Expressions | PHP 8.5's `|>` applies a callable resolved at run time; this one substitutes `$_` in the parser, so the emitted tree is the nested spelling's and no closure is allocated | [`expressions/pipeline-substitution`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-pipeline-substitution) |
| Expressions | PHP has no expression-level `catch`; a one-line fallback for a throwing call is a language form rather than a swallowed `@` or a five-line block | [`expressions/catch-expression`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-catch-expression) |
| Expressions | PHP's `@` is gone, and the one-liner that would regrow it is named at compile time instead | [`expressions/bare-throwable-arm-warns`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-bare-throwable-arm-warns) |
